” (liquid or flow), refers to all the stuff that Hashem “pours down” on you from birth (e.g., where you were born, when you were born, who your parents are, your talents and handicaps — both physical and emotional) and all the stuff that happens in life (e.g., the people He arranges you to meet, winning lotteries,

getting cancer, etc.). All these things are the tools He gives you so you can fulfill your many particular jobs on this earth. Perhaps your job is to be that poor person who makes the correct choice to be happy with what he has and be an inspiration to others (rather than making the incorrect choice of being cranky and angry). In addition, poor people provide others with the opportunity to do the mitzvah of tzedakah. Someone needs to be poor; without poor people, how would everyone else be challenged between an evening watching dumb videos or volunteering for Tomchei Shabbos? Needing Tomchei Shabbos packages is an important job — and Hashem chose you!Of course, someone also needs to be rich so they’ll have to deal with deciding whether to waste five thousand dollars on a watch no one will ever see or to give that amount to Tomchei Shabbos. That’s also an important job! Same goes with being sick or healthy, having stable parents or growing up in a dysfunctional home, or being the kid who tutors others or the one who gets tutored!
